[{"sha":"63bd920445f5339aa0ccaf07475df7abac2c8632","node_id":"C_kwDOAHR-9doAKDYzYmQ5MjA0NDVmNTMzOWFhMGNjYWYwNzQ3NWRmN2FiYWMyYzg2MzI","commit":{"author":{"name":"Matt Caswell","email":"matt@openssl.foundation","date":"2026-10-19T09:58:18Z"},"committer":{"name":"Tomas Mraz","email":"tomas@openssl.foundation","date":"2026-10-21T09:21:35Z"},"message":"Don't report held-back DTLS app data as readable in SSL_poll()

ossl_dtls_conn_poll_events() reported SSL_POLL_EVENT_R whenever
SSL_has_pending() was true. For DTLS that includes records in
buffered_app_data, which dtls1_read_bytes() only releases once the
handshake has finished.

In DTLS 1.3 the sender of a KeyUpdate stays in init until it is ACKed.
If the peer sends application data without ACKing, e.g.:

  1. Server sends KeyUpdate, enters TLS_ST_SW_KEY_UPDATE.
  2. Client sends a record before reading the KeyUpdate.
  3. Server's SSL_read() buffers the record, returns WANT_READ.

then every SSL_poll() returns at once with SSL_POLL_EVENT_R and every
SSL_read() returns SSL_ERROR_WANT_READ. An event loop spins until the
ACK arrives or the KeyUpdate retransmissions run out (483s). The same
happens to a client, and in DTLS 1.2 for data received between
ChangeCipherSpec and Finished.

Only count buffered_app_data once the handshake has finished, and
otherwise wait for incoming datagrams as usual.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-QCQMEE2S).

Caswell","email":"matt@openssl.foundation","date":"2026-10-19T08:14:08Z"},"committer":{"name":"Tomas Mraz","email":"tomas@openssl.foundation","date":"2026-10-20T13:29:57Z"},"message":"Don't dereference a NULL rbio in dtls1_read_failed()

Connections created by a DTLS listener have no read BIO; they read
from a queue that the listener's demux fills. dtls1_read_failed()
still set BIO_FLAGS_READ on the read BIO unconditionally once the
handshake had finished.

A DTLS 1.3 server keeps its retransmission timer armed after the
handshake until the client ACKs the NewSessionTickets. A client that
never sends that ACK can arrange for the timer to expire while a
non-blocking SSL_read() on the server is pumping the demux and finds
no record (for example, by sending datagrams the record layer
discards). dtls1_read_bytes() then calls dtls1_read_failed(), which
crashes on the NULL BIO.

Skip setting the flag when there is no read BIO. SSL_get_error()
already returns SSL_ERROR_WANT_READ for listener connections without
one.

The DTLS listener has not been in any final release, so no released
version of OpenSSL is affected.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-NPC3SFSW).

Caswell","email":"matt@openssl.foundation","date":"2026-10-19T08:37:48Z"},"committer":{"name":"Tomas Mraz","email":"tomas@openssl.foundation","date":"2026-10-20T12:38:12Z"},"message":"Clear the next pointer when inserting into an empty pqueue

pqueue_pop() leaves the popped item's next pointer intact. If that item
is then inserted into an empty queue, pqueue_insert() kept the stale
pointer, which links back into the queue it came from.
dtls1_clear_sent_buffer() does exactly this with its temporary queue. If
it then frees the item that the stale pointer refers to, the freed item
is reached again when the temporary queue is drained.

DTLS 1.3 has not been in any final release, so no released version of
OpenSSL is affected.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner (finding ANT-2026-YZ5U4MXB).
